title: Apparent memory in dynamics comes from omitted variables

statements.text: Apparent history dependence, such as memory kernels or non-Markovian effective dynamics, arises when a coarse description omits dynamically relevant variables. Enlarging the state to include them restores a dynamically sufficient description, so the theorem does not need every effective model to be memoryless.

sources.quote: Apparent dependence on history commonly arises only because an effective or coarse-grained description omits dynamically relevant variables.
